global.q: What is the difference between assisted living, memory care and a care home?
global.a: Assisted living helps with bathing, dressing, meals and medications in a private apartment. Memory care is a secured unit with dementia-trained staff for people who may wander or cannot be left alone safely. Care home is the everyday name for either one.

global.q: How do I choose a senior care home in Memphis?
global.a: Settle four things in order: the care your parent needs today, whether memory loss needs a secured unit, what the family can pay for years, and fit. Tour only the communities that pass the first three.

global.q: How many licensed assisted living communities are there in the Memphis area?
global.a: Tennessee's July 2026 bed report lists 31 licensed Assisted Care Living Facilities in Shelby County, 23 with secured memory care beds. Mississippi's October 2026 directory lists 6 licensed Personal Care Homes in DeSoto County, 2 with dementia care units.

global.q: What does Tennessee license assisted living as?
global.a: Tennessee licenses assisted living as an Assisted Care Living Facility through the Tennessee Health Facilities Commission. Memory care units sit inside those facilities and are counted as secured beds. Nursing homes and homes for the aged hold separate licences.

global.q: When is it time for memory care?
global.a: When dementia makes your parent unsafe: wandering or trying to leave, getting lost in familiar places, or not being safe alone. A diagnosis by itself is not the trigger; safety is.

global.q: Is memory support the same as memory care?
global.a: No. Memory support usually means a programme of activities inside ordinary assisted living with no secured unit. Ask whether the community has secured beds on its licence.

global.q: How much does assisted living cost in Tennessee?
global.a: CareScout's 2025 survey put the annual median cost of assisted living in Tennessee at $67,140, against $74,400 nationally. Memphis-area communities price above and below that depending on apartment, location and care level, so ask for an all-in quote in writing.

global.q: What does the monthly rate include?
global.a: Usually the apartment, three meals a day, utilities, housekeeping, activities and scheduled transport. Care is often charged on top by level, along with fees for medication management, incontinence supplies and escorts.

global.q: Why did the quote go up after the assessment?
global.a: The advertised price is usually the base rate. The assessment sets your parent's care level, and each level adds a monthly care charge. Ask which tasks set the level and what would move it up.

global.q: What are activities of daily living?
global.a: Bathing, dressing, eating, using the toilet, staying continent, and moving from bed to chair. Communities assess help with each, plus medications and memory, to set a care level and price.

global.q: Does Medicare pay for assisted living?
global.a: No. Medicare pays for doctors, hospital care, therapy, prescriptions and short skilled nursing stays after a qualifying hospital stay. It does not pay rent, meals or personal care in assisted living or memory care.

global.q: Does TennCare pay for assisted living?
global.a: TennCare CHOICES can pay for care services in an Assisted Care Living Facility for people who qualify, up to $1,497.77 a month in 2026. It does not pay room and board, which the resident pays from income, capped at $2,385.60 a month for CHOICES members.

city.q: How many licensed assisted living communities are there near {{marketLabel}}?
city.a: The directory on this page lists every Assisted Care Living Facility the Tennessee Health Facilities Commission licenses in Shelby, Tipton and Fayette Counties and every Personal Care Home the Mississippi State Department of Health licenses in DeSoto and Marshall Counties, sorted by distance from {{marketLabel}}.

city.q: Which communities near {{marketLabel}} have memory care?
city.a: Communities marked Memory care report secured beds to Tennessee, or hold a licensed Alzheimer's and dementia care unit in Mississippi. A secured unit is a locked or alarmed area for residents who may wander. Ask each community how many secured beds are open now.

city.q: What is the difference between a care home and assisted living?
city.a: People use care home loosely for any residential setting. In Tennessee, an Assisted Care Living Facility is licensed to help with daily activities and medications; a residential home for the aged offers room, board and supervision only; a nursing home provides 24-hour skilled nursing.

city.q: How do I know whether my parent needs assisted living or memory care?
city.a: If your parent needs help with bathing, dressing or medications but is safe on their own, assisted living usually fits. If they wander, get lost, or cannot be left alone safely because of dementia, a secured memory care unit is the safer choice.

city.q: Does Medicare pay for assisted living near {{marketLabel}}?
city.a: No. Medicare does not pay for long-term custodial care in assisted living. It can cover a short skilled-nursing stay after a qualifying hospital stay. Tennessee residents may qualify for help with care costs through TennCare CHOICES.

city.q: How quickly can a parent move in after a hospital stay?
city.a: Some communities can assess and admit within a few days if a room is open and the paperwork is ready. Have the discharge summary, medication list, physician orders and a TB screening ready to speed it up.

city.q: Is this guide free for families in {{marketLabel}}?
city.a: Yes. Families never pay us. Senior living communities pay us a referral fee or a flat fee when they accept a family we introduce, and some buy sponsored placements, which are labelled.

city.q: How do I check a community's inspection history?
city.a: Use the licence number in the directory to look the community up with the Tennessee Health Facilities Commission, which publishes licensure and survey information. Ask the community for its most recent survey and how any deficiencies were corrected.

city.q: What should I bring to a tour near {{marketLabel}}?
city.a: Bring your parent's medication list, a short note on what help they need each day, and your budget range. Use the 40 questions checklist in our guides so every tour is compared the same way.

city.q: Can my parent keep their own doctor after moving?
city.a: Usually yes. Most assisted living residents keep their own physician, though some communities have visiting doctors or nurse practitioners. Ask how appointments and transport are handled.

city.q: Are DeSoto County and West Memphis communities included?
city.a: DeSoto County, Mississippi communities are included from the Mississippi State Department of Health directory. Arkansas licenses assisted living through its own agency and is not yet listed, so families in Crittenden County see the nearest Tennessee and Mississippi communities.
